bi-report.main: Production-grade AWS QuickSight–driven analytics and reporting platform designed for large-scale educational environments, combining embedded BI, multi-tenant access control, database-driven analytics modeling, and aggressive session cost optimization.

summary.a: Embedded analytics platform fully integrated into the application UI using secure QuickSight embed flows.
summary.b: Designed for large-scale reporting workloads across thousands of schools and administrative users.
summary.c: Database views, analytics modeling, and query tuning used to support high-frequency operational reporting.
summary.d: Snapshot-based rendering strategy reduced projected QuickSight session cost by approximately 90%.

system-scale.data-volume: Five years of historical incident data with hundreds of thousands of records, including operational metadata, incident classification, timestamps, school and facility information.
system-scale.usage-traffic: Thousands to tens of thousands of daily report views across approximately 30 reports and 10+ visualization types.

report-categories.attendance: Student attendance tracking, staff check-in / check-out logs, late arrival monitoring, and tardiness analytics.
report-categories.incident-monitoring: Vaccination reporting, infection tracking, facility exposure logging, and date / district / school-based aggregation.
report-categories.summary: Role-based dashboards providing school-only or district-wide analytical views depending on user scope.

data-platform.analytics-logic: Complex business rules, aggregations, and reporting transformations were implemented at the RDS layer using database views to reduce BI dataset complexity and stabilize query patterns.
data-platform.bi-layer: Simple report-specific expressions were delegated to QuickSight calculated fields, keeping the visualization layer lightweight and avoiding unnecessary duplication of heavy aggregation logic.
data-platform.platform: Reporting workloads were isolated from the transactional path through view-based models, SPICE usage, and dedicated read-oriented strategies to support operational analytics without destabilizing OLTP behavior.

performance-opt.heavy-report-opt: Expensive district-wide joins were reduced by isolating school metadata into DynamoDB and synchronizing relational metadata into a read-optimized structure.
performance-opt.spice: Daily summary reports were moved to SPICE with scheduled refresh, eliminating unnecessary real-time query load on the source database.
performance-opt.query-tuning: Composite indexes, execution plan analysis, join restructuring, and view-based query shaping reduced dashboard latency and improved overall reporting responsiveness.

design.a: Reports were built in QuickSight and embedded into the application using secure URLs generated through .NET API and Lambda orchestration.
design.b: Access control was enforced through API-level authorization, role-aware filtering, and parameterized tenant scoping for school-level and district-level users.
design.c: This architecture maintained secure multi-tenant isolation while keeping the reporting experience fully embedded.

strategy.a: QuickSight session pricing made high-frequency report access operationally expensive at scale.
strategy.b: A snapshot rendering pipeline was introduced: if a requested report snapshot already existed, the platform served the cached visual output instead of creating a new BI session.
strategy.c: Headless browser capture + S3 storage dramatically reduced session creation while preserving visual equivalence for non-interactive report scenarios.

impact.performance: Maintained around 3-second average dashboard response time.

header.title: SQL Tuning Advisor
header.desc: Designed and implemented an automated SQL tuning system by reverse-engineering Oracle SQL Tuning Advisor. The system analyzes slow SQL and generates optimization recommendations including SQL Profile, index suggestions, statistics fixes, and SQL rewrites.

overview.title: Overview
overview.desc1: Oracle SQL Tuning Advisor is an automated SQL performance analysis and optimization system provided by Oracle Database.
overview.desc2: This project reverse-engineered that workflow and implemented an Oracle-style SQL tuning automation framework, including task lifecycle management, advisor metadata tables, analysis modules, report generation, and SQL Profile acceptance flow.
overview.desc3: In practical terms, this can be understood as an advanced internal system that automates EXPLAIN analysis + optimizer tuning + recommendation generation.

purpose.title: Purpose
purpose.desc: The key objective of this project was not just manual SQL tuning, but automation of SQL tuning workflows: converting optimizer knowledge and performance diagnostics into a repeatable advisor system that can create, execute, analyze, and report tuning tasks.

stat.title: 1. Statistics Analysis
stat.desc: Detects stale or missing statistics that lead to incorrect execution plans.

profiling.title: 2. SQL Profiling
profiling.desc: Compares estimated vs actual row count patterns and generates profile-based recommendations to improve optimizer decision quality.

access.title: 3. Access Path Analysis
access.desc: Evaluates whether Full Scan or Index Scan is more appropriate and suggests access-path improvements.

structure.title: 4. SQL Structure Analysis
structure.desc: Detects query patterns that degrade performance and provides rewrite recommendations.

purpose.title: Purpose
purpose.desc: Implemented an Oracle-style SQL Tuning Advisor by reverse engineering internal architecture, including task lifecycle, analysis modules, recommendation logic, report generation, and SQL Profile acceptance flow.

milestone.c: • Design advisor packages, system tables, and views
milestone.d: • Build tuning task execution and report generation system

feature.e: • Expensive operation detection (NOT IN, UNION, join issues)

package.title: 1. Package Design
package.desc: The advisor was designed around multiple internal packages, following the Oracle-style separation between public APIs, internal execution logic, and low-level utility subprograms.

item1.a: • Public package that exposes the main advisor lifecycle APIs
item1.b: • Includes procedures/functions for CREATE, EXECUTE, REPORT, and ACCEPT SQL PROFILE
item1.c: • Serves as the main user-facing interface for tuning task management

item2.a: • Internal execution package responsible for the detailed analysis steps during tuning task execution
item2.b: • Encapsulates advisor workflow logic such as statistics analysis, access path analysis, and structural SQL checks
item2.c: • Separates internal execution behavior from the public package API

item3.a: • Utility package for subprograms that need lower-level implementation
item3.b: • Designed to isolate logic better suited for C/C++-level implementation
item3.c: • Helps keep advisor package logic modular and maintainable

table.title: 2. System Tables
table.desc: The advisor required dedicated system metadata tables created during DB booting, along with DBA-style views for visibility into definitions, tasks, objects, executions, and logs.

system_tables.definitions: • ADVISOR_DEFINITIONS: Stores metadata for advisor categories such as ADDM, SQL Access Advisor, Undo Advisor, SQL Tuning Advisor, and SQL Workload Manager
system_tables.tasks: • ADVISOR_TASKS: Stores and manages each advisor execution unit as a task
system_tables.objects: • ADVISOR_OBJECTS: Stores task-related objects by object_id and object_name
system_tables.logs: • ADVISOR_LOGS: Records step-by-step logging of advisor execution and tuning progress

table.footer: This metadata layer was critical for implementing task lifecycle persistence, execution traceability, and report generation

create.title: 3. Create Tuning Task
create.a: • Accepts user inputs such as sql_id, scope, task_name, time_limit, and related tuning parameters
create.b: • Generates default values for missing optional inputs
create.c: • Performs validation checks on input arguments
create.d: • Persists validated inputs and generated metadata into advisor system tables
create.e: • Establishes the initial lifecycle state of the tuning task

execute.title: 4. Execute Tuning Task
execute.desc: The execution phase was designed as a multi-step analysis pipeline that automatically inspects optimizer-related causes of SQL performance issues.

stat.a: • Detects missing or stale statistics on tables and indexes
stat.b: • Identifies cases where poor optimizer estimates may be caused by statistics quality issues

access.a: • Evaluates whether current access paths are cost-optimal with and without indexes
access.b: • Generates guidance on access path improvement
access.c: • Can recommend running SQL Access Advisor when index-oriented design changes are needed

structure.a: • Detects query patterns known to cause performance degradation at syntax / semantic analysis stage
structure.b: • Recommends replacing NOT IN with NOT EXISTS
structure.c: • Recommends replacing UNION with UNION ALL where appropriate
structure.d: • Detects datatype mismatch between indexed columns and WHERE clause predicates
structure.e: • Detects missing join conditions that indicate design mistakes or hidden Cartesian effects

report.a: • Aggregates advisor findings from execution logs, analysis output, and recommendation records
report.b: • Produces structured tuning reports for users
report.c: • Summarizes actionable items such as statistics collection, SQL rewrite, alternative plan, and SQL Profile usage
report.d: • Designed as the final user-facing output of the tuning task lifecycle

profile.a: • Supports applying approved SQL Profile recommendations to the target SQL
profile.b: • Connects advisor recommendation results to optimizer execution behavior
profile.c: • Bridges analysis output with actual runtime performance improvement

summary.b: • Internal Execution Layer: DBMS_SQLTUNE_INTERNAL package for advisor pipeline and analysis execution
summary.c: • Utility Layer: C/C++-oriented utility package for low-level subprogram support
summary.d: • Metadata Layer: Advisor system tables and DBA views for definitions, tasks, objects, logs, and executions
summary.e: • Recommendation Layer: Statistics, access path, structural rewrite, and SQL Profile recommendation generation<

conclusion.a: This project demonstrates more than SQL tuning itself: it demonstrates the design and implementation of an automated SQL tuning system that models advisor lifecycle, analysis workflow, metadata persistence, recommendation generation, and optimizer-facing profile application.
conclusion.b: It also highlights hands-on experience in C++, PL/SQL, database internals, optimizer behavior, and performance engineering.

erp-replatform.main: Re-architected a legacy fashion ERP — where data was scattered across PKL/JSON files and consistency kept breaking — onto a single-source-of-truth, 5-layer reference architecture, and owned a phased, zero-downtime migration strategy. Defined the data contracts, builder standard, and snapshot model that turned a pile of one-off scripts into a governed pipeline.
erp-replatform.loc: Role: Architect & sole implementer — owned architecture, migration strategy, data contracts, and delivery end to end.

summary.a: Adopted single-source-of-truth as a first principle to eliminate a whole class of consistency failures — every report reads the DB, not files, retiring the PKL/JSON dependency axis.
summary.b: Defined a 5-layer reference architecture (Raw → Cleansed → Marts → Snapshot → Outputs) so every new report follows the same governed flow with no exceptions.
summary.c: Separated immediacy (HTML) from time-series analytics (snapshots) by design — dual-writing outputs and absorbing analytics needs at the contract level via a -current / -trend / -history query contract.
summary.d: Codified a three-layer split of presentation, I/O, and compute as the frontend standard — a repeatable tab-development convention the team can follow verbatim.

system-scale.codebase: A single-owned production codebase spanning backend, data pipeline, and frontend (~130K LOC, 403 commits) with clearly defined layer boundaries and ownership.
system-scale.database: One PostgreSQL 16 instance, 97 tables layered along raw/cleansed/snapshot boundaries and unified under products.id as the canonical key — establishing a single authority for the data model.
system-scale.surface: 26 API boundaries, 25 domain services, 36 frontend views, and 148 pipeline scripts operated consistently on one DB contract.

principles.ssot: Designed every builder to use only the DB → memory → output path via a shared loader — removing the file-cache shortcut entirely so consistency is guaranteed by architecture, not operational discipline.
principles.snapshot: Split outputs into volatile views and durable snapshots and defined a standard query contract (-current / -trend / -history) — absorbing time-series needs into design at the contract level.
principles.buildless: Chose a bundler-free CDN Vue 3 + scoped-CSS standard — a deliberate architectural trade-off that removes build-pipeline and dependency-management complexity from operations.

performance.oom: Root-caused a full production outage (host OOM) to an architectural anti-pattern — a shared, monolithic in-memory model — and re-architected to per-domain bounded loaders, established as a design rule applied to every tab thereafter, not a one-off patch.
performance.codec: Identified serialization as the system throughput bottleneck and redesigned the codec strategy — cutting core-path latency several-fold (dev-measured 32.9s → 5.6s) and reclaiming capacity headroom.
performance.cache: Designed a service-cache layer with version-stamp invalidation — removing repeated recomputation and structurally lowering read cost (dev-measured 30s → 0.4s).

pipeline.a: Designed NAS ingestion as idempotent, incremental loads with per-batch failure isolation (minimized blast radius) — so one bad file never halts the whole pipeline.
pipeline.b: After a column-shift incident, introduced an ingestion contract and validation gate — a defensive design that converts silent data corruption into fail-fast.
pipeline.c: Time-separated builder scheduling with real-time observability (sub-step monitor) built in — treating operational visibility as an architectural requirement.

frontend.a: Defined a convention that forces the View to be a shell and presentation to be components — a structural guardrail against single files owning multiple responsibilities.
frontend.b: Standardized charts/data as client-initialized and decoupled from server outputs — letting the presentation layer evolve independently of data generation.
frontend.c: Banned the shared monolith in favor of per-tab bounded loaders while reusing canonical formulas — a design that delivers autonomy and consistency at once.

impact.reliability: Guaranteed data consistency by architecture rather than operational discipline — structurally removing the failure classes of file dependence, key mismatch, and format errors
impact.performance: Redesigned core paths to retire latency and capacity risk, and codified regression-prevention rules alongside (dev-measured)
impact.scale: Converged into an integrated platform running 97 tables, 36 views, and 148 scripts consistently on one source of truth
impact.arc: Owned — at the strategy level — the re-architecture and phased migration from a file-based monolith to a snapshot-oriented single source of truth

agent-platform.main: Designed an operating model to scale and govern AI-assisted engineering on top of a live production ERP. Split agent responsibility along product-domain boundaries (Conway-aligned), and established defense-in-depth safety governance plus a persistent-knowledge system that compounds across sessions — an orchestration layer built on top of Claude Code.
agent-platform.loc: Role: Designer of the operating model — defined and implemented the agent org structure, governance, and knowledge architecture.

summary.a: Designed agent responsibility to map 1:1 onto product-domain boundaries — an org structure (Conway-aligned) that contains a change's blast radius within its domain.
summary.b: Defined a skill layer that routes work as identify → delegate → regression-verify — standardizing so a process, not a person, allocates work.
summary.c: Designed a layered persistent-knowledge system (domain, system contracts, learned feedback) so organizational knowledge compounds across sessions.
summary.d: Designed three-tier, defense-in-depth governance (policy, confirmation, hard block) that structurally controls the risk of irreversible and production-impacting actions.

system-scale.agents: 42 agents with per-domain responsibility boundaries — domain ownership and change isolation implemented at the org level.
system-scale.skills: 16 skill routers — repeatable work standards that codify identify → delegate → verify.
system-scale.memory: 59 knowledge artifacts — organizational memory layered into terms/rules (domain), system contracts (service), and learned feedback.

pillars.mapping: Isolated responsibility via 1:1 agent-domain mapping (bounded contexts) — designing org boundaries so work in one domain doesn't spill into another.
pillars.meta: Designed a meta-framework (agent-blueprint) that stamps out the standard system (skills + agents + knowledge + commands) for any new domain from a canonical template — making the practice itself scalable.
pillars.knowledge: Designed a learning loop that persists feedback as knowledge — preventing recurrence of the same mistake by process, not personal memory.

governance.policy: Continuously enforces intent-level risks that command patterns can't catch (production-data edits, mass sends) — the first line of governance.
governance.gate: Controls hard-to-reverse actions (commit/push, container ops, deletes) with pre-execution confirmation — inserting human approval into the workflow as a contract.
governance.hardblock: Blocks irreversible commands by default (force push, reset, drop, production-network access), allowing only time-boxed exceptions — a hard gate enforcing least privilege and explicit exceptions.

review.a: Designed review to inspect only the diff in an isolated worktree — scoping review by contract.
review.b: Parallelized four dedicated perspectives (intent, quality, layer, data) and integrated them — structurally removing single-viewpoint blind spots.
review.c: Separated authoring from review into distinct passes (separation of duties) — categorically forbidding same-context self-approval.

memory.a: Domain-knowledge layer — canonicalizes terms, boundaries, rules, and shared dependencies to preserve business context in the system.
memory.b: System-contract layer — maps the provenance of screens, APIs, DB, and response keys into architecture knowledge that can be checked against code.
memory.c: Learning layer — session handovers and accumulated feedback guarantee continuity of long-running work and organizational memory.

impact.velocity: Achieved parallel, consistent execution across a large codebase at the org level via per-domain agents and process routing
impact.safety: Structurally controls the accident risk of production/irreversible actions through defense-in-depth governance
impact.knowledge: Built a learning system where organizational knowledge compounds across sessions over 59 persistent artifacts
impact.arc: Designed and established a self-extending engineering operating model that treats AI as a first-class actor
